# Introduction

::: {.callout-tip title="Video lecture"}
David Rocke's Epi 204 lecture
[*Poisson Regression*](https://dmrocke.ucdavis.edu/Class/EPI204-Spring-2021/EPI204-2021-04-22.mp4)
([slides](https://dmrocke.ucdavis.edu/Class/EPI204-Spring-2021/EPI204-8%20Poisson%20Regression.pdf))
covers Poisson regression with a log link and a population [offset](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/distributions.html#def-offset),
rate ratios,
residual diagnostics,
goodness of fit,
and [overdispersion](#def-overdispersion),
using Danish lung cancer incidence data
[@rocke2021epi204].
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Video lecture"}
Richard McElreath's
[*Modeling Events*](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=RuBUVQELw-c)
(Statistical Rethinking 2026, Lecture A09)
accompanies Chapters 10 and 11 of @statrethink2e,
which cover generalized linear models for binary and count outcomes,
including Poisson regression.
The lecture fits these models using [Bayesian inference](https://morrison-lab.github.io/sds/bayesian-inference.html#def-bayesian-paradigm)
rather than the [maximum likelihood estimation](https://morrison-lab.github.io/sds/intro-MLEs.html#def-mle) used in this chapter
[@mcelreath2026rethinking].
:::

## Negative binomial models

::: notes
There are alternatives to the Poisson model when overdispersion is present.
Most notably,
the [negative binomial model](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/distributions.html#sec-nb-dist).
:::

Diagnostics that reveal [overdispersion](#def-overdispersion) are telling us
that the data violate the standard Poisson assumption

$$\Var{Y \mid \vX=\vx, T=t} = \E{Y \mid \vX=\vx, T=t}$$

Ignoring that violation leads to artificially narrow [standard errors](https://morrison-lab.github.io/sds/estimation.html#def-SE)
and inflated type I error rates.
The [negative binomial distribution](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/distributions.html#sec-nb-dist)
serves as a natural generalization of the [Poisson distribution](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/distributions.html#def-poisson)
for count outcomes.
It introduces an overdispersion parameter $\rho$
that allows the [conditional variance](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/variance-covariance.html#def-cond-variance) to exceed the mean
($\Var{Y \mid \vX=\vx, T=t} = \mu(\vx, t) + \mu(\vx, t)^2 / \rho$).
We still model $\mu(\vx, t) = t \exp{\eta(\vx)}$ as before,
preserving the rate-ratio interpretation for regression coefficients.
Furthermore, negative binomial models can be combined with zero-inflation
to account for both structural zeros and variance expansion in count data,
with the negative binomial serving as the conditional distribution
for the count component.
